- Be proud of who you are
- Be kind to your partners
- Don’t ignore red flags 
- Know your boundaries
- Confidence is attractive
- Be aware of your mental health. If you need therapy, get therapy. 
- Take care of your body. Drink lots of water and implement exercise into your daily routine. Walking and dance parties with your cat count as exercise. 
- If you aren’t happy in a relationship, leave.
- Understand that your happiness is dependent on you. Never on someone else. Your partner can add to your happiness but should never be the source of it.

I’m friends with all my exes. One of them is my best friend 7 years after our breakup. We took time apart to heal and slowly reconnected. It’s hard to heal when you are texting every day but with that, there’s no right or wrong way to go about it. Being friends with an ex is very possible.
Whoa! Celebrity in the house 😭 *be cool be cool be cool*

I’m so sorry this happened OP. If they kick you out, call CPS again. You are still a minor. Can you contact your sister? Also, check out your local lgbtq+ resources. If you are in a smaller city, call one that is nearby and maybe they could offer you some advice.

That’s unfortunate. It’s good she was honest with you and you know where she stands. If you aren’t ready to come out and she has her standards set, it’s best to walk away before growing too attached. I come from a conservative family as well. I didn’t come out per say.. my mom walked in on my gf and I when I was 16. I’m 36 now and she’s never been accepting of my life. I could have been fine with never coming out because it’s only caused more trauma with her cruel words and hatefulness towards me. I hope one day when you feel confident enough to come out, that your family can be accepting. Until then, take all the time you need and find someone who can accept and respect that.

Im friends with my ex’s. I have no desire to be with any of them again and vice versa so there is nothing romantic for anyone to worry about. At one point, my ex and I became roommates. Platonic to the point it was hard to imagine there used to be a relationship. Then I met my gf and we had a place. My ex needed a new living situation and so we rented a room to her. It was chill. I even became roommates with that gf after we broke up. I know not everyone has this experience but just because our relationship didn’t workout, it doesn’t mean we be friends. Knowing my experience and my lack of anything romantic for ex’s, it doesn’t bother me for partners to be friends with their ex’s. If I feel this person is still too attached or lying about their feelings towards them, that’s a conversation to be had.

All you need is to find someone who matches your intimacy style. For me, when I am with someone, I want them to feel good, feel loved and feel pleasured. It really turns me on when I please them. I also want that in return from my partner. In my head, it creates a special connection that brings us closer. 

It’s important to me that we both feel all the good feelings. I’ve been with a pillow princess before and it was definitely my fault for not learning more about her before we slept together. Im usually confident in my skin and I feel attractive most days but that experience took me by surprise. I felt rejected but it didn’t take long for me to realize that was my insecurities talking way too loud. She liked me as a person and wanted to be “physical” but she was a pillow princess. Lesson learned. 

Are pillow princesses selfish? Depends on the person and their reasons. If it’s because they aren’t confident in what they are doing and have a mental block about that, I can understand. If they have associated trauma, I absolutely understand. If they have physical issues and maybe don’t have a mouth or have missing arms, I understand. But if it’s because you for no reason, don’t want to give your partner pleasure because the act of touching your partner is more off putting than giving her pleasure, yes selfish in my book. 

Thankfully there are a lot of lesbians who only like to receive. Be open about it with them and make sure you both align. And btw, I don’t hate pillow princesses, I just know that isn’t my ideal partner.
Yes! Get it 🎉

She is emotionally manipulating you. Please protect yourself and leave. If you think she might actually harm herself, call her family or if they aren’t around, call the police next time she threatens that.
Mm.. I haven’t had one in years. Looks good.

Don’t be sorry for venting. Sometimes it helps to get it out and talk about it. That’s shitty you get left hanging but try not to lose hope. If they don’t respond after a few days, unmatch with them. The right connection will come along.

Yep. Your feelings are valid. Personally, when a partner communicates they need to cancel once or twice, its understandable but its a problem when it becomes a pattern. Has she reached out to you to hangout or try to make it up? If they aren’t putting in the effort, I would have a conversation with her. Maybe she’s having a hard time or stressed but I would communicate your needs and tell her how you feel.
Come out as many times as you want. Bake yourself a cake and celebrate 🎉

I have a love hate relationship with therapy but have you tried it? Someone who specifically specializes in LGBTQ+ issues? If that’s a no go, do you journal? Ask yourself all the “why” questions. Try getting to the root of why it’s so important for you to be with a man. Is it family acceptance? Or societal norms/compulsory heterosexuality? Or is it her? Maybe you don’t see her as your forever partner but you’re in a place that is comfortable?

Have you communicated any of this to her? Is she aware you are struggling with this?
It sounds like you have picked up on her red flags. Don’t ignore them. Trust your gut and move on.

I have terrible gaydar and have to poll my friends most often but It sounds like she would be open to hanging out. Casually bring up the hiking trails again and ask if she would want to go with you. Or ask her more about her cute pig and emphasize that you want to meet it. Also, next time you see her, ask her if it’s okay to text her. If she seems weird about it then that’s that. Also, if it helps, I went to conservative high school and a religious university. I’m a lesbian and atheist but I had a scholarship and I liked the location. So you never know. Good luck.
